To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a simple pre-operative evaluation of total serum proteins, beta-globulines, and C3c serum levels coupled with skin testing reactivity to intracutaneous injection of Multitest, is a reliable test for the identification of patients at high risk for post-operative infections.

a) the combination of total serum protein and albumin levels with the score of skin test reactivity is a good predictor of septic complications after surgical treatment of digestive tract cancer; b) the predictive power of this test is high enough to be considered a valid screening tool for the identification of patients at high risk for septic infections; c) the use of this test might allow the surgeon to select a subgroup of patients for a more aggressive pre-operative nutritional support.

(i) the pre-operative identification of patients "at risk" for septic complications is feasible and useful; (ii) the best discriminant equation is based on serum total proteins with electrophoreses and skin test reactivity; (iii) the sensitivity of this equation is 67%, specificity is 88% and positive predictivity is 76%; (iv) this equation should be used to select patients for a more aggressive pre-operative nutritional support.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the pre-operative assessment of the nutritional and immunologic status of patients with cancer, in order to identify those patients at "septic risk".
the development of a new method of pre-operative evaluation for the identification of patients at "septic risk".

the development of a simple, reliable, and reproducible test to be used in the pre-operative identification of "septical risk" patients, in order to allow the surgeon to take appropriate preventive measures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the pre-operative evaluation of nutritional status (serum proteins, albumin, beta-globulines and C3c) and of the immunocompetence (skin testing) is a reliable and valid method for the identification of patients at "septic risk".
a combination of skin testing and serum proteins assay is useful in the identification of patients at high risk for developing post-operative infections.
a simple, reliable and inexpensive method for the pre-operative identification of "sepsis risk" patients has not been yet developed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combination of skin testing with serum protein assessment is a reliable tool for pre-operative selection of patients at risk of post-operative infection.

a pre-operative assessment of serum proteins, electrophoresis and skin test reactivity might be useful to select "septic risk patients" in order to plan an appropriate peri-operative nutritional and/or immunologic support.

a low serum albumin level, low serum beta-globulines, low serum C3c, and low skin test score to recall antigens may represent useful parameters for the selection of patients at high risk of post-operative infection.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the pre-operative identification of septic risk patients is possible by a combination of anthropometric and laboratory parameters.
the pre-operative assessment of nutritional status, immunologic parameters, and skin test reactivity may be a useful tool to identify patients at risk for post-operative infections.

the skin test reactivity, as well as the serum protein level, may be useful for the selection of "sepsis risk" patients, but that the combination of the two parameters is more reliable than either one of them alone.
